case.pattern_description: Coordinated cross-card exploitation orchestrated via a specific Android profile (Samsung SM-G935F on Chrome) operating behind anonymous proxies across at least 20 cards. The perpetrator executes 1 to 2 card-not-present transactions per compromised account to remain below standard velocity thresholds and avoid elevated model scores. Previous investigations into this exact device and infrastructure were confirmed fraudulent and classified under Policy R9 as undocumented coordinated abuse.

evidence.claim: Device D004630 (SM-G935F Build/NRD90M | Android 7.0 | chrome 62.0 for android | 1920x1080) was used across 20 distinct cards between 2016-10-23 and 2016-11-22, appearing as a new device behind an anonymous proxy for every single card.

Device D004630 is linked to four prior closed cases (CC-2649, CC-2985, CC-2971, CC-3035), all confirmed fraud under the undocumented pattern where cardholders reported unauthorized purchases from this exact device profile behind an anonymous proxy.
The flagged transaction 3478561 and prior online transaction 3460634 were conducted using device D004630, marked as New for this account and operating behind an anonymous proxy.

Card C13487-K1 is predominantly used for in-person transactions on product W (69 of 71 lifetime transactions, and 15 of 17 in the past 30 days). The two online product C transactions (3460634 for $112.37 and 3478561 for $74.96) deviate sharply from normal holder channel and product usage.
Transactions 3460634 ($112.37) and 3478561 ($74.96) occurred 7 days apart with amounts well above the typical in-person purchase amounts of $25 to $36 seen on card C13487-K1.
The fraud model assigned a score of 0.006 with a historical fraud rate of 0.006 to flagged transaction 3478561, and risk score was 0.05.
Flagged transaction 3478561 is associated with region 191, which is one of the card's two primary historical billing regions with 36 prior transactions.

evidence.claim: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

Rule R6: Shared origin: Rule R6: Shared origin. When several cards show fraud from the same device profile, the same billing region, or the same recipient email in one window, name the shared element, recommend `CREATE_CASE` and `FILE_REPORT`, and `MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS` for every card that shares it.

case.summary: An investigation was opened following an analyst request regarding suspicious activity on card C13487-K1 linked to a shared device profile. Flagged transaction 3478561 ($74.96) and prior transaction 3460634 ($112.37) were conducted online via device D004630 behind an anonymous proxy, sharply deviating from the holder's established history of in-person retail transactions. Graph analysis revealed that device D004630 was linked to 20 cards in the past 30 days and tied to four prior confirmed fraud cases (CC-2649, CC-2985, CC-2971, CC-3035) operating under the same undocumented pattern. Although model scores remained low, this matches the perpetrator's pattern of coordinated abuse keeping amounts low to evade detection. With an assessed fraud probability of 0.81, a case was opened, 19 connected cards were queued for monitoring, and the matter was escalated to an analyst under policies R6 and R9.
